pages.text: A focus can $(italic)have$() multiple influences, but may only $(italic)be$() the influence of up to one other focus. However, in some situations, a focus is a valid influence for multiple "target" foci. So how do the spirits choose?

When choosing between multiple targets, a focus looks at each possible target's $(bold)influence outflow$(): the number of foci the target could potentially influence minus the number of foci that could potentially influence the target. Multiple targets with the same outflow are ignored. The remaining one with the highest outflow is chosen.

When holding chalk and looking at a focus, you may notice smaller dimmer circles. These represent potential influences (blue) and targets (orange) that $(italic)do$() have valid symmetry, but were $(italic)not$() chosen due to the principle just outlined.
